statement: Reserve succeeds for any positive whole quantity up to and including the available quantity, returns a reservation with a unique id, and the reserved units stop being available.

faults.description: Reservation ids stop advancing, so consecutive reservations share the same id.
The new reservation is never stored, so available stock does not drop and release of the returned id throws UnknownReservation.
Off-by-one in the stock check rejects a reservation for exactly the available quantity with InsufficientStock.

statement: Reserve rejects a zero, negative or fractional quantity with InvalidQuantity and an unknown SKU with UnknownSku, leaving stock unchanged.

faults.description: The quantity validation call is removed, so a zero quantity creates a reservation.
The unknown-SKU check is disabled, so an unknown SKU fails with InsufficientStock instead of UnknownSku.

statement: Sweep expires every active reservation whose expiry is at or before the given time, including one expiring exactly at that time, and returns the count.

faults.description: A reservation expiring exactly at the sweep time is no longer expired.
The comparison loses its right-hand operand, leaving a source file that cannot be parsed.

statement: Receive adds a positive whole quantity to on-hand, registering a new SKU, and accepts only SKUs of 3 to 12 uppercase letters, digits or hyphens.

faults.description: The default for a not-yet-registered SKU is removed, so receiving a new SKU throws a TypeError.
The SKU length limit is removed, so SKUs longer than 12 characters are accepted.
The SKU pattern test is forced off, so malformed SKUs are registered instead of failing with InvalidSku.

statement: WriteOff reduces on-hand by the given quantity but never below the currently reserved total; a request that would do so fails with InsufficientStock and changes nothing.

faults.description: The protective check written against an older variable name, forced off so over-write-offs pass.
faults.find: if (current - quantity < this.reservedOf(sku)) throw new InsufficientStock();

faults.description: The reserved-total floor is replaced by zero, so on-hand can drop below reserved stock.
A write-off increases on-hand instead of reducing it.

statement: An order of 100 or more units gets an extra 5% on top of the customer-type discount, summed and not compounded, with percentage discounts rounded half up to a whole cent.

faults.description: The bulk percentage becomes a string, so for member bulk orders the percentages concatenate into a wrong percent.
Rounding half up is replaced by truncation, so 1851.75 rounds to 1851.
The customer-type set is never constructed, so pricing any order throws a TypeError.
faults.replace: const types = null as unknown as Set<CustomerType>;

statement: stockReport counts only active reservations as reserved, reports status "low" for 1 to 9 available and "ok" from 10, and returns an entry for every known SKU.

faults.description: Released reservations keep counting toward reserved (first of two matches is replaced).
Ten available units are reported as "low" instead of "ok".
The entries array is undefined, so stockReport throws a TypeError whenever any SKU is registered.
faults.replace: const entries: StockEntry[] = undefined as unknown as StockEntry[];

statement: reportTotals returns the SKU count and the sums of onHand, reserved and available across all SKUs, and all four are 0 with no SKUs.

faults.description: The reserved total sums available quantities instead of reserved quantities.
The SKU count is pinned to 1 whenever at least one SKU exists.
The onHand total keeps only the last SKU's quantity instead of summing.
